implementation_constraints: Pure Python stdlib only: json, re, shlex, sys
Reads a single JSON object from stdin
Verdict is process exit code only: 0 allow, 2 block
Fail-closed on malformed JSON, unexpected input shape, and shell commands that cannot be proven read-only

unresolved_intent.decision: Recognize common read-only tool names exactly after lowercasing and removing separators, including read, grep, glob, ls, list, dir, find, search, web fetch/search, and notebook read variants.
unresolved_intent.rationale: The package names tool families but not host-specific identifiers, so the implementation uses conservative common aliases for readers, searchers, listers, web fetch/search, and notebook readers without matching broad write-capable names.

unresolved_intent.decision: Treat Bash, shell, sh, command, terminal, cmd, powershell, and pwsh style tool names as shell/command tools.
unresolved_intent.rationale: The package gives Bash as an example and says shell/command tools may vary by host, so common command-execution tool names are handled with the shell policy.

unresolved_intent.decision: Consider a shell command proven read-only only when every pipeline/sequence stage has a read-only executable and no redirection, assignment-like write option, or tee-like/file-writing command appears.
unresolved_intent.rationale: The package requires default-deny for shell commands touching .approved files and specifically calls out later pipeline writers, redirection, and in-place/output write flags.

unresolved_intent.decision: If shlex parsing fails, the command is blocked when it contains the .approved marker.
unresolved_intent.rationale: A parse failure means the guard cannot prove read-only, and the posture is fail-closed.

unresolved_intent.decision: Allow unknown non-shell tools when their argument tree contains no .approved marker.
unresolved_intent.rationale: The invariant concerns approved golden files; the package specifically says unknown tools block when the marker appears anywhere in arguments, leaving calls that do not mention approved goldens outside the protected surface.
